residencyRequirements.description: At least one party must have been a resident of Kentucky for at least 180 days (approximately 6 months) before filing. The petition is filed in the county where the petitioner resides. There is no separate county residency requirement.

waitingPeriod.description: Kentucky has a mandatory 60-day waiting period. The decree cannot be entered until at least 60 days have elapsed after the petition is filed. KRS 403.170(1).

noFault.name: Irretrievable Breakdown
noFault.description: The marriage is irretrievably broken. May be established by both parties affirming the breakdown, one party stating it and the other not denying it, or the parties living apart for at least 60 days.

groundsForDissolution.notes: Kentucky is a pure no-fault state. The only ground for dissolution of marriage is irretrievable breakdown. Fault is not considered in granting the dissolution.

propertyDivision.description: Kentucky divides marital property in 'just proportions,' considering the contribution of each spouse to acquisition of marital property (including the contribution of a spouse as homemaker), the value of property set apart to each spouse, the duration of the marriage, and the economic circumstances of each spouse at the time of the division.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Non-marital (separate) property includes property acquired before marriage, property acquired by gift or inheritance during marriage, property acquired in exchange for non-marital property, and property excluded by valid agreement.

filingFees.notes: Kentucky filing fees for dissolution of marriage range from approximately $115 to $185 depending on the county. Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals via a Motion to Proceed In Forma Pauperis.

basic.name: Case Data Information Sheet (VS-300)
basic.description: Vital statistics form required by Kentucky courts

basic.name: Verified Disclosure Statement
basic.description: Mandatory disclosure of income, assets, and debts
basic.notes: Required by Kentucky Family Court Rules

basic.name: Decree of Dissolution of Marriage
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

service.name: Summons
service.description: Formal service on respondent by sheriff or certified process server
alternatives: Entry of Appearance and Waiver of Service

service.name: Entry of Appearance and Waiver of Service
service.description: Respondent voluntarily accepts service and enters an appearance
service.notes: Must be signed by respondent and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Parenting Time Agreement / Schedule
withChildren.notes: Required in most Kentucky family courts

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Kentucky Rules of Civil Procedure

inState.description: Respondent must file an answer within 20 days of service

outOfState.description: Respondent served outside Kentucky must file an answer within 20 days of service (may be extended by the court)

responseDeadlines.statute: Kentucky Rules of Civil Procedure, CR 12.01

childSupportGuidelines.description: Kentucky uses an income shares model. Both parents' combined monthly adjusted parental gross incomes are used to determine the basic child support obligation from a schedule. The obligation is apportioned between the parents based on their proportional share of the combined income.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if application would be unjust or inappropriate. Adjustments for childcare, health insurance, and extraordinary expenses.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Kentucky courts may award maintenance (not alimony) when one spouse lacks sufficient property to provide for reasonable needs and is unable to support themselves through appropriate employment. There are no statutory formulas — the court exercises broad discretion based on the statutory factors in KRS 403.200.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: The court considers: financial resources of the party seeking maintenance, time needed to acquire education/training, standard of living during marriage, duration of marriage, age, physical and emotional condition, and the ability of the paying spouse to meet their needs while paying maintenance.

court.name: Family Court / Circuit Court
court.description: Dissolution of marriage is filed in the Family Court (in counties where Family Court has been established) or the Circuit Court (in counties without a Family Court) in the county where the petitioner resides.
